3. $h\ell - k\ell + hm - km - hn + kn =$

A. $(h + k)(\ell - m + n)$
B. $(h + k)(\ell + m - n)$
C. $(h - k)(\ell - m + n)$
D. $(h - k)(\ell + m - n)$
reasoning: Factor by grouping: h\ell - k\ell = \ell(h - k), hm - km = m(h - k), and -hn + kn = -(hn - kn) = -(h - k)n. Thus the whole expression equals (h - k)(\ell + m - n), which corresponds to option D.
